jobs.title: vIOP Clinical Quality Supervisor
jobs.description:
About Lyra

Lyra Clinical Associates partners with Lyra Health, a leading provider of evidence-based mental health care, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Lyra members have access to care in one day, and nine out of ten improve with the support of providers like you. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions. You will be employed by Lyra Clinical Associates.

About The Role

We are looking for an experienced mental health clinician and leader with a passion for clinical care, quality, supervision, and management to serve as a clinical quality supervisor for our Pediatric virtual Intensive Outpatient Program (vIOP), an accelerated, comprehensive care experience that helps young people ages 7 to 25 feel better quickly from the comfort of home. The pediatric vIOP is a critical service for acute patients who need more than traditional, once-a-week therapy. This program is a critical component of our full-spectrum of care services. It not only helps to avoid re-hospitalization, but its availability within our services ensures these members have direct access to our core coaching, therapy, and psychiatry services once they are stabilized.

As a vIOP Clinical Quality Supervisor you will spend half the time delivering direct client care and half the time providing management oversight and clinical supervision to vIOP Associate Social Worker (ASW) therapists.

Direct client care:
You will provide time-limited, evidence-based treatment via telehealth. You’ll conduct individual, family, and group skills training sessions, maintaining a caseload of diverse and varied clinical needs. You’ll conduct psych urgent care individual sessions as needed, which consists of risk and safety assessments and developing stabilization plans. An important note: Clients come from a multitude of different backgrounds and experiences, and have varying needs and abilities. We strive to continue to meet their unique needs by delivering culturally responsive care–an approach that accounts for the impact of cultural backgrounds on each person’s care experience.

Clinical supervision and management:
You will help train, manage, and supervise a team of ASW therapists utilizing CBT, DBT, ERP and other evidence-based practices to support vIOP clients through our innovative video therapy platform. This includes reviewing and providing feedback on clinical quality metrics and consulting on clinical cases. You will also assist with quality improvement initiatives including specialty consultations, provider training, and quality assurance reviews.

Regularly:
Our vIOP team members enjoy connecting with peers, who share a passion for providing evidence-based care. You’ll attend one-on-one clinical consultation, multidisciplinary team meetings, and robust training to enhance your clinical and supervision skills. You’ll always have access to expert consultation and support for your most complex clients. It’s like a safety net of resources to help plan the best options–from specialty consultations to culturally responsive care–you’re not alone, even while working remotely within the US.

This role is a great fit
if you have experience supporting pediatric and young adult clients with mood and anxiety disorders in a high acuity (IOP, PHP, residential) setting using evidence-based and culturally responsive practices, as well as supervising and managing registered ASW’s.

This role reports to our vIOP Clinical Quality Manager.

Key Responsibilities

Maintain a caseload of vIOP clients, vIOP group sessions, and/or Psych Urgent Care appointments (14 bookable calendar spots)
Support recruiting, interviewing, onboarding, and training of vIOP ASW therapists
Provide clinical quality oversight, mentoring, clinical and administrative supervision to vIOP ASW therapists in clinical practice
Provide ongoing feedback regarding ASW therapists’ performance including clinical quality, productivity, adherence to evidence-based treatment models, client feedback, and interpersonal effectiveness;
Ensure care provided across the team is culturally responsive and outcomes-driven;
Lead ongoing clinical 1:1’s and consultation team meetings with assigned vIOP ASW therapists and consultation teams;
Provide clinical coverage for vIOP individual and group sessions as needed;
Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Master’s degree from a clinical social work track (LCSW) from an accredited program
Current unrestricted license to practice in California
Willingness to obtain cross-licensing in additional states as needed to support program growth
5+ years postgraduate clinical experience
Experienced in providing care in a high acuity (IOP, PHP, residential) setting
Highly skilled in working with clients with severe, co-occurring clinical diagnoses and high risk presentations
Highly skilled in providing evidence-based treatments (e.g., CBT, DBT, ERP, ACT, TF-CBT, etc.)
Experienced and passionate about helping kids, teens, young adults, and families to achieve goals
Experienced in brief, goal-focused psychotherapy using measurement based care
2+ years of experience in clinical supervision/training of evidence based therapies
Prior administrative management
Grounded in cultural humility with a commitment to culturally responsive care
Experience with video therapy and providing supervision/consultation on how to conduct clinical sessions via video conferencing software
Comfort with technology and working within a fast-moving environment
Excellent interpersonal skills (listening and communicating)
Passion for transforming mental health through technology with a human touch
Availability to work afternoon and evening hours. Must be able to work 11am-8pm Pacific Time, Monday-Friday;
Potential opportunity to work Saturdays;
Ability to work full-time, approximately 40 hours per week;
Full-time resident of the United States

Shall provide supportive services to households experiencing homelessness in order to maximize housing stability and prevent returns to homelessness. Shall provide direct assistance in gaining access to services, coordination of care, oversight of the entire case, and linkage to appropriate services. The overall goal of the position is to help individuals and families quickly exit homelessness and return to permanent housing through a tailored package of assistance that may include the use of time-limited financial assistance and targeted supportive services.

Responsibilities

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Represent The Salvation Army, the church and service programs in a professional and caring manner.
Maintain client confidentiality at all times.
Provide case management to households referred to the Rapid Rehousing program including, but not limited to, intake/assessment, housing location/inspection, lease negotiation, goal setting/tracking, service planning, referrals, linkage to community-based services, discharge planning, and financial assistance based upon HUD/CoC guidelines, available resources, and policies and procedures of The Salvation Army.
Promote access to and effective utilization of mainstream benefits, such as transportation assistance, income and non-income benefits, and SSI/SSDI technical assistance.
Provide services consistent with a Housing First, strengths based, harm reduction and trauma informed approach.
Maintain face to face contact with clients at least monthly and phone contact with clients as frequently as needed.
Review service plans monthly and update at least every three months.
Document all contacts and attempted contacts with a client via a case note within two business days.
Complete annual assessments in HMIS within 30 days before or after the anniversary of the date of engagement.
Maintain confidential and accurate client files with all required documentation and detailed case notes in compliance with the policies and procedures of The Salvation Army, HUD/CoC and all other funders.
Enter required information in the HMIS database within two business days.
Assist with helping clients obtain transportation to appointments.
Achieve the following annual program outcomes: At least 81% of households will maintain their housing or exit to another permanent housing placement, At least 45% of households will increase their income, Households should move into permanent housing within an average of 30 days.
Produce and submit statistical reports in a timely manner.
Participate in continuous quality improvement reviews.
Network with community agencies and participate in collaborative networks such as the CoC to stay current on services available, explore potential partnerships, and to address issues that are relevant to the community.
Participate in staff meetings, trainings, conferences and other professional development opportunities for social services/technical skills improvement.
Refer clients seeking spiritual guidance to the Corps Officers.

A Bachelor’s degree in Human Services or related social services field.
At least two years of experience in a housing, behavioral health or crisis-oriented program which includes one year involvement with the homeless.

Knowledge of homelessness, mental health, drug and alcohol, and crisis intervention is

Position Overview

The Community Educator supports Jewish Family Service of San Diego’s Immigration Legal Services team by expanding community outreach, immigrant education, and access to immigration legal resources throughout San Diego County and the surrounding region. Working under the supervision of the Assistant Director of Immigration Operations and Partner Coordination, this position helps connect immigrants, mixed-status families, schools, nonprofit partners, and community-based organizations with trusted legal information, social services, and community resources.

The Community Educator strengthens community partnerships, delivers Know Your Rights presentations, coordinates immigration legal services walk-in clinics at K-12 schools and community sites, participates in outreach events, and helps immigrants and mixed-status families navigate legal and social service referrals. This position may participate in intensive training to become a U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) partially accredited representative. Upon accreditation, and as program capacity allows, the Community Educator may assist with selecting immigration matters under appropriate supervision. The role also serves as a liaison between JFS, nonprofit partners receiving community education funding through the Regional Network Hub for Immigrant Families, and the communities JFS serves. Through community engagement, client navigation, legal services support, documentation, and administrative coordination, the Community Educator helps increase awareness of immigration and social services, promote equitable access to immigration legal assistance, and support the broader goals of the JFS Immigration Services team.

Responsibilities

Develop, implement, and evaluate outreach strategies for communities most impacted by immigration enforcement, including border communities, immigrant-dense neighborhoods, mixed-status families, newly arrived populations, and other priority communities identified by the program.
Plan, coordinate, and deliver Know Your Rights presentations, community education workshops, informational sessions, and resource presentations for immigrant communities, service providers, schools, faith groups, community-based organizations, and partner agencies in both in-person and virtual formats.
Coordinate and respond to Regional Network Hub (RNH) community education requests, including presentations, tabling events, workshops, and resource fairs.
Provide accurate, accessible, and culturally responsive information about immigration processes, available legal services, community resources, and referral pathways through ILSC, ILSD, and partner organizations.
Coordinate immigration legal services walk-in clinics at K-12 schools and community sites, including scheduling, partner communication, outreach, intake flow, interpretation coordination, volunteer support, materials preparation, and follow-up referrals.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with community-based organizations, schools, faith-based institutions, immigrant-serving agencies, local government partners, and other stakeholders to expand access to immigration legal education and services.
Support recruitment, engagement, communication, and relationship-building efforts with community partners participating in Regional Network Hub activities and initiatives.
Serve as a liaison between JFS, Regional Network Hub-funded nonprofit partners, and community partners to support alignment, communication, referrals, reporting, and community education goals.
Review incoming community education requests and coordinate with Regional Network Hub partners to identify the most appropriate organization or educator to fulfill each request.
Coordinate presentation and outreach logistics, including scheduling, materials preparation, partner communication, site coordination, interpretation needs, and follow-up activities.
Represent the Immigration Legal Services team at community meetings, partner convenings, outreach events, school-based events, resource fairs, trainings, and other public-facing forums.
Assist individuals and families in accessing legal consultations, screenings, referrals, and representation through ILSD and partner programs, with a focus on detained, recently released, enforcement-impacted, and at-risk populations.
Conduct initial intake, issue spotting, eligibility screening, and client navigation, and connect potential clients with appropriate internal programs, external legal providers, social services, and emergency resources.
As capacity allows, assist ILRP attorneys and DOJ-accredited representatives with immigration court filings, briefs, declarations, legal research, document collection, client communication, case preparation, and other case-related support.
Support short-term representation efforts by identifying potential clients, preparing referral information, coordinating follow-up, and connecting individuals with legal staff supporting ILSC services and other appropriate resources.
Upon DOJ partial accreditation, and under appropriate supervision, provide legal screenings, conduct preliminary legal analysis, assist with immigration forms and filings within the scope of accreditation, and support limited or short-term representation before DHS as program capacity permits.
Support accompaniment to ICE check-ins, ISAP appointments, immigration appointments, court-related appearances, and other scheduled immigration-related appointments as capacity permits and in accordance with program protocols.
Collaborate with legal, outreach, advocacy, and communications staff to develop, review, translate, update, and distribute Know Your Rights materials, handouts, flyers, resource guides, presentations, and community education tools.
Track, document, and report outreach activities, clinic participation, presentations, referrals, client contacts, partner engagement, and other required program data accurately and in a timely in accordance with grant, program, and agency requirements.
Submit and track community education activities, presentations, outreach events, and partner engagement data in the ILRC Data Portal and other required reporting systems.
Maintain organized records, outreach calendars, contact lists, attendance records, referral logs, data entry, and other documentation needed for program monitoring, reporting, and evaluation.
Attend ILSC monthly meetings, Regional Network Hub convenings, community meetings, trainings, internal team meetings, and other required meetings to stay informed on immigration policy changes, community needs, program priorities, and partner activities.
Support the planning, coordination, outreach, registration, and follow-up activities related to Regional Network Hub convenings and partner meetings.
Stay current on rapidly changing immigration laws, policies, enforcement trends, agency procedures, local resources, and community concerns, and help communicate relevant updates to staff, partners, and community members in an accessible manner.
Support social media, outreach, and communications efforts related to community education, clinic promotion, legal updates, public education campaigns, and community resources as needed.
As capacity allows, answer live calls, respond to callback requests, conduct basic triage, provide resource information, and route callers appropriately through the ILSC hotline or other designated program communication channels.
Assist with scheduling, reminders, follow-up calls, interpretation coordination, document requests, appointment preparation, and other client communication needs.
Support the recruitment, onboarding, coordination, training, and day-to-day guidance of volunteers, interns, interpreters, and community ambassadors assisting with outreach, clinics, hotline support, and community education activities.
Participate in program planning, evaluation, quality improvement, and implementation of new outreach or service delivery models to better meet community needs.
Comply with all agency policies, confidentiality requirements, data protection standards, grant requirements, legal ethics rules, and professional boundaries applicable to the position.
Perform additional case management, community engagement, administrative, and program support duties as assigned to meet the evolving needs of the Immigration Legal Services team.

Skills/Experience/Abilities That Are a Must-Have

Eligible and willing to apply for U.S. Department of Justice partial accreditation.
Valid California driver’s license, access to reliable vehicle for transportation, personal vehicle insurance, and ability to travel for work-related duties.
High school diploma or equivalent required; associate or bachelor’s degree in social work, legal studies, ethnic studies, public policy, education, nonprofit management, or a related field preferred. Equivalent lived and professional experience may be considered.
Commitment to social justice, immigrant rights, and serving vulnerable, marginalized, and enforcement-impacted communities.
Passion for providing culturally competent, trauma-informed, accessible, and community-centered outreach and education to immigrant and newcomer populations.
Experience conducting community outreach, public speaking, presentations, workshops, trainings, or community education, preferably with immigrant, refugee, or mixed-status communities.
Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to engage diverse audiences, explain complex information clearly, and build trust with community members and partners.
Bilingual proficiency in Spanish, Arabic, Farsi, Haitian Creole, Portuguese, or other languages commonly spoken by immigrant communities in the region strongly preferred.
Knowledge of immigration rights, enforcement issues, removal defense, humanitarian relief, and border-region dynamics preferred; willingness and ability to learn is required.
Ability to travel throughout San Diego and Imperial counties for outreach, clinics, meetings, appointments, and community events.
Comfort working independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, community-focused, and mission-driven environment.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, records, and reporting requirements.
Flexibility to work evenings and weekends to meet community outreach, clinic, and partner needs.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams, and familiarity with virtual meeting platforms such as Zoom and Teams.
Experience working with marginalized populations, survivors of trauma, and individuals navigating complex legal, social service, or crisis situations.
Ability to maintain confidentiality, exercise sound judgment, follow supervision, and communicate professionally with clients, partners, volunteers, and colleagues.
Experience with data entry, case management systems, outreach tracking, grant reporting, or client records preferred.

Physical Requirements

Occasional evening and weekend work may be required.
Regular local travel may be required for community events, school-based clinics, partner meetings, client appointments, trainings, court-related support, and other program activities.
While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to sit, talk, listen, use a computer, operate office equipment, and communicate by phone, video, and in person.
The employee frequently needs to stand, walk, reach, use hands and fingers to operate a keyboard, handle documents and outreach materials, and move between office, clinic, and community event settings.
The work environment may include office settings, schools, community sites, public events, and other off-site locations. Noise levels may vary and may require the ability to concentrate and communicate effectively.
The employee must be able to lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds as needed for outreach materia

This position may participate in intensive training to become a U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) partially accredited representative. Upon accreditation, and as program capacity allows, the Community Educator may assist with selecting immigration matters under appropriate supervision. The role also serves as a liaison between JFS, nonprofit partners receiving community education funding through the Regional Network Hub for Immigrant Families, and the communities JFS serves. Through community engagement, client navigation, legal services support, documentation, and administrative coordination, the Community Educator helps increase awareness of immigration and social services, promote equitable access to immigration legal assistance, and support the broader goals of the JFS Immigration Services team.

Responsibilities

Develop, implement, and evaluate outreach strategies for communities most impacted by immigration enforcement, including border communities, immigrant-dense neighborhoods, mixed-status families, newly arrived populations, and other priority communities identified by the program.
Plan, coordinate, and deliver Know Your Rights presentations, community education workshops, informational sessions, and resource presentations for immigrant communities, service providers, schools, faith groups, community-based organizations, and partner agencies in both in-person and virtual formats.
Coordinate and respond to Regional Network Hub (RNH) community education requests, including presentations, tabling events, workshops, and resource fairs.
Provide accurate, accessible, and culturally responsive information about immigration processes, available legal services, community resources, and referral pathways through ILSC, ILSD, and partner organizations.
Coordinate immigration legal services walk-in clinics at K-12 schools and community sites, including scheduling, partner communication, outreach, intake flow, interpretation coordination, volunteer support, materials preparation, and follow-up referrals.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with community-based organizations, schools, faith-based institutions, immigrant-serving agencies, local government partners, and other stakeholders to expand access to immigration legal education and services.
Support recruitment, engagement, communication, and relationship-building efforts with community partners participating in Regional Network Hub activities and initiatives.
Serve as a liaison between JFS, Regional Network Hub-funded nonprofit partners, and community partners to support alignment, communication, referrals, reporting, and community education goals.
Review incoming community education requests and coordinate with Regional Network Hub partners to identify the most appropriate organization or educator to fulfill each request.
Coordinate presentation and outreach logistics, including scheduling, materials preparation, partner communication, site coordination, interpretation needs, and follow-up activities.
Represent the Immigration Legal Services team at community meetings, partner convenings, outreach events, school-based events, resource fairs, trainings, and other public-facing forums.
Assist individuals and families in accessing legal consultations, screenings, referrals, and representation through ILSD and partner programs, with a focus on detained, recently released, enforcement-impacted, and at-risk populations.
Conduct initial intake, issue spotting, eligibility screening, and client navigation, and connect potential clients with appropriate internal programs, external legal providers, social services, and emergency resources.
As capacity allows, assist ILRP attorneys and DOJ-accredited representatives with immigration court filings, briefs, declarations, legal research, document collection, client communication, case preparation, and other case-related support.
Support short-term representation efforts by identifying potential clients, preparing referral information, coordinating follow-up, and connecting individuals with legal staff supporting ILSC services and other appropriate resources.
Upon DOJ partial accreditation, and under appropriate supervision, provide legal screenings, conduct preliminary legal analysis, assist with immigration forms and filings within the scope of accreditation, and support limited or short-term representation before DHS as program capacity permits.
Support accompaniment to ICE check-ins, ISAP appointments, immigration appointments, court-related appearances, and other scheduled immigration-related appointments as capacity permits and in accordance with program protocols.
Collaborate with legal, outreach, advocacy, and communications staff to develop, review, translate, update, and distribute Know Your Rights materials, handouts, flyers, resource guides, presentations, and community education tools.
Track, document, and report outreach activities, clinic participation, presentations, referrals, client contacts, partner engagement, and other required program data accurately and in a timely in accordance with grant, program, and agency requirements.
Submit and track community education activities, presentations, outreach events, and partner engagement data in the ILRC Data Portal and other required reporting systems.
Maintain organized records, outreach calendars, contact lists, attendance records, referral logs, data entry, and other documentation needed for program monitoring, reporting, and evaluation.
Attend ILSC monthly meetings, Regional Network Hub convenings, community meetings, trainings, internal team meetings, and other required meetings to stay informed on immigration policy changes, community needs, program priorities, and partner activities.
Support the planning, coordination, outreach, registration, and follow-up activities related to Regional Network Hub convenings and partner meetings.
Stay current on rapidly changing immigration laws, policies, enforcement trends, agency procedures, local resources, and community concerns, and help communicate relevant updates to staff, partners, and community members in an accessible manner.
Support social media, outreach, and communications efforts related to community education, clinic promotion, legal updates, public education campaigns, and community resources as needed.
As capacity allows, answer live calls, respond to callback requests, conduct basic triage, provide resource information, and route callers appropriately through the ILSC hotline or other designated program communication channels.
Assist with scheduling, reminders, follow-up calls, interpretation coordination, document requests, appointment preparation, and other client communication needs.
Support the recruitment, onboarding, coordination, training, and day-to-day guidance of volunteers, interns, interpreters, and community ambassadors assisting with outreach, clinics, hotline support, and community education activities.
Participate in program planning, evaluation, quality improvement, and implementation of new outreach or service delivery models to better meet community needs.

Perform additional case management, community engagement, administrative, and program support duties as assigned to meet the evolving needs of the Immigration Legal Services team.

Eligible and willing to apply for U.S. Department of Justice partial accreditation.
Valid California driver’s license, access to reliable vehicle for transportation, personal vehicle insurance, and ability to travel for work-related duties.
High school diploma or equivalent required; associate or bachelor’s degree in social work, legal studies, ethnic studies, public policy, education, nonprofit management, or a related field preferred. Equivalent lived and professional experience may be considered.

Job Overview

Fairview is looking to hire an Acute Care Social Worker to join our team at Fairview - University Hospital in Minneapolis, MN. This is a 0.6 FTE, benefit-eligible position, working three days per week (six days per pay period). The schedule includes an every sixth weekend rotation and one holiday per calendar year.

The Acute Care Social Worker plays an important role in supporting patients and families throughout their hospital stay by addressing psychosocial needs, coordinating resources, and collaborating with the interdisciplinary care team to support safe and effective discharge planning.

The acute social worker works on-site with the interdisciplinary teams including providers, physical therapists, nurses, dieticians, chaplains and pharmacists to assist patients and families in navigating through their hospitalization. The acute social worker completes psychosocial assessments, care planning/ progression and creates comprehensive discharge plans from the hospital. The social worker is patient facing, responds to crisis situations, manages patient and family expectations, creates solutions to identified discharge barriers and aims to reduce length of stay and prevent avoidable hospital readmissions.

Addresses social determinants of health and assists with connecting patients to needed resources in the community such as chemical dependency treatment, domestic violence resources, housing stabilization services, mental health services, food shelves, transportation, financial assistance etc.
